issues: Inside the frame was a grey skeleton: placeholder bars instead of an interface, nothing real to read in the window
The dashboard was transform-scaled into the window with its bottom row cut in half, reading like a wireframe
A flat grey ground inside the frame with no depth at the edge, so the frame read as a colour block rather than a mat
The window drop had no motion blur and a fixed shadow; the flip had no motivation (nobody pressed a toggle) and felt like a timer
Blue and green had similar lightness and the band labels were tiny (under 24px), so the flip was weakly legible
changes: Look = porcelain (cool white stage); the frame is the only strong colour: Design cobalt #2F55FF ↔ Dev orange #FF5B1F, opposed hues plus a lightness gap; the UI itself is neutral ink and accents follow the mode

The subject is now a shot-designed window of a fictional design tool, Tessel (1560×864 native pixels): layers panel, a canvas with a big pricing card ($24 at 124px), and an inspector, with the Start free trial button selected

Four things hard-cut on the same flip frame: frame colour, band label DESIGN→DEV MODE, toggle state, and the whole layout (light inspector → dark CSS code panel, layers → tokens, blue selection → orange redlines)

Added motivation: a cursor arcs to the Design | Dev toggle in the title bar, presses with anticipation and releases on the flip frame; the flip gets a 3-frame radial flash, a damped band-thickness bounce and a ~1% content jolt

Retimed to 140f: 0–18 frame grows to 60px (visible by frame 2) → 10–40 window springs in (18° tilt settling, velocity blur, tightening shadow) → 36–52 selection handles pop in staggered → 84 flip → 86–104 redlines draw on 3f apart with overshooting value pills → hold with a 2% slow push
